etymologies.etymologyHTML: Borrowed from Latin exclūdō, from prefix ex- (“out”) + variant form of verb claudō (“close”).

definitions.definition: (transitive) To bar (someone or something) from entering; to keep out.

quote.citation: 1960 December, “New G.E. Line diesel loco maintenance depot at Stratford”, in Trains Illustrated, page 766:
quote.text: One end of the east-west building is wet, the other windy, and at present there is smoke abounding, too; but these distressing yard elements can be completely excluded at each end by full-width folding doors [...].

quote.citation: 2019 July 24, David Austin Walsh, “Flirting With Fascism”, in Jewish Currents‎[1]:
quote.text: [T]he 1924 Immigration Act was designed specifically to exclude Eastern European Jews (among other undesirable European ethnic groups) from entering the country.

quote.citation: 1669, John Baptiſta Porta, chapter V, in Natural Magick‎[2], The Third Book Of Natural Magick:  […] , page 68:
quote.text: […]  for hungry birds have devoured ſeeds, and having moiſtened and warmed them in their bellies, a little after have dunged in the forky twiſtes of Trees, and together with their dung excluded the ſeed whole which erſt they had ſwallowed: and ſometimes it brings forth there where they dung it,  […]

definitions.definition: (transitive, law) To refuse to accept (evidence) as valid.
(transitive, medicine) To eliminate from diagnostic consideration.
